content: I want to build a Node.js AI router CLI tool
Great idea. Let's start with the project structure. We'll need Express for the HTTP layer and a provider adapter system.
I want to use SQLite for storing conversation history
Good choice. We'll use node:sqlite, the built-in Node.js SQLite module. No extra dependencies needed.
Which port should Express run on?
Let's use localhost:3000 as the default. Users can override it with an environment variable.
I've finished db.js and router.js. What's next?
Now build commands.js to handle the CLI commands, then the provider adapters for Groq, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
There's a bug — the Gemini model name is wrong
Change it from gemini-pro to gemini-1.5-flash. Google renamed their models.
Also Groq decommissioned one of the models we were using
Switch to llama3-8b-8192 — it's their current stable free model.
Commands.js is done too. How should I structure the provider adapters?
Each provider should be a module that exports a single callProvider function with the same signature. That way the router doesn't need to know which provider it's calling.
I prefer clean function names and no inline comments
Noted. Clean names, comments only in block form where truly necessary.
All adapters done — Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek
Great. Now let's refactor the provider architecture to use a cleaner routing pattern.
How should I handle Ollama for local model authentication?
Ollama doesn't require authentication by default on localhost. We'll handle it as a special case — no API key required, just a base URL.
Should the router auto-retry on rate limit?
Yes. Catch 429 errors and switch to the next provider automatically. That's the core value proposition of ai-router.
What's the best way to handle conversation history in the router?
Currently we use a sliding window — keep last 10 messages. But we're planning to replace this with MemoryDistil for structured compression.
Now let's start the provider architecture refactor
Let's begin. First, extract all provider logic into a providers/ directory with a clean index that routes by provider name.
